newsitem.title: FRANCE: French May 5 lorry protesters say trouble unlikely.
newsitem.headline: French May 5 lorry protesters say trouble unlikely.

text.p: A day of action by French lorry drivers on May 5 is unlikely to lead to serious disruption to traffic on French roads, union representatives told Reuters.

"We see this day of action as reminder to road transport bosses that some of the points in the agreement they signed with us last November (which brought to an end a 12-day strike) have yet to be honoured," an official of the CFDT union's transport branch said.
The agreement encompassed guarantees on pay, working conditions and retirement at 55 years.
"Action will probably centre on distributing pamphlets at motorway toll gates to get our case across rather than an out-and-out blockade of highways," the official added.
A spokesman for the CGT union echoed these comments.

"We are not looking to trigger off a strike such as in November 1996. There may be a little disruption to traffic here and there but the day of action is more a nudge to bosses to get their act together vis-a-vis the agreement they signed," he said.
The spokesman said coach drivers and public transport personnel would also be joining the protest.
